candidate.title: scATAC-Seq (Cell Index)
candidate.scope: The assigned Illumina schematic for combinatorial cellular indexing scATAC-Seq, interpreted using Cusanovich et al. (2015), PMID 25953818. One target workflow is depicted. The three representative wells in each round are retained as distinct local transformations; they are not actual plate sizes or additional target methods. The left single-cell and nucleosome vignette introduces accessible chromatin, and the route ends at pooled indexed DNA. Routine unshown execution steps and alternative scATAC implementations are outside scope.

states.label: Pooled indexed DNA library
features: Parallel DNA lines with colored end segments are the final depicted product. No exact end chemistry or index sequence is specified by these icons.

Sequencing the chromatin-derived DNA fragments supplies genomic locus information; the combination of first-round Tn5 and second-round PCR well identities associates fragments with a putative cell and supports a sampled chromatin accessibility profile.

The primary paper describes preferential insertion into nucleosome-free chromatin and barcode collisions in which more than one nucleus receives the same index combination; these limit accessibility specificity and single-cell attribution.
